questions.question: You must walk 10,000 steps a day to see health benefits.
questions.answer: False - Research shows that walking as few as 7,000 steps daily can significantly reduce health risks.

questions.question: Walking doesn't help with weight loss.
questions.answer: False - Walking burns calories and, combined with a healthy diet, supports weight loss.

questions.question: You need to walk for 30 minutes straight to gain benefits.
questions.answer: False - Multiple short walks, such as three 10-minute sessions, are just as effective.

questions.question: Brisk walking isn't as effective as running.
questions.answer: False - Brisk walking improves cardiovascular health and is gentler on the joints compared to running.

questions.question: Walking is only for beginners or those who can't run.
questions.answer: False - Walking is beneficial for all fitness levels and can be intensified with techniques like power walking.

questions.question: You must walk at a fast pace to reap health benefits.
questions.answer: False - Even moderate walking speeds provide health benefits; consistency matters most.

questions.question: Walking doesn't improve mental health.
questions.answer: False - Regular walking reduces stress, anxiety, and depression, enhancing mental well-being.

questions.question: Walking is boring and monotonous.
questions.answer: False - Walking can be enjoyable with music, podcasts, or exploring new routes.

questions.question: Walking doesn't build muscle.
questions.answer: False - Walking tones leg and core muscles and can improve bone density.

questions.question: Walking is not a real workout.
questions.answer: False - Walking is a legitimate form of exercise that improves cardiovascular health and aids in weight management.
